text: Top Dance Albums, previously known as Top Electronic Albums and later as Top Dance/Electronic Albums, is a weekly music chart published by Billboard magazine that ranks the top-selling dance music albums in the United States based on sales data collected by Nielsen SoundScan. The chart first appeared on the June 30, 2001, issue under the title Top Electronic Albums, with the original soundtrack to the film Lara Croft: Tomb Raider holding the first number-one position. It initially consisted of fifteen positions and has since expanded to include twenty-five albums. The chart includes full-length albums by artists associated with electronic dance music genres such as house, techno, IDM, and trance, as well as pop-oriented dance music and electronic-leaning hip hop. Remix albums by non-electronic artists and DJ-mixed compilation albums or film soundtracks featuring a majority of electronic or dance music are also eligible. In 2019, Billboard introduced a companion chart, Dance/Electronic Album Sales, which ranks the top 15 albums based exclusively on physical sales, focusing on core dance/electronic artists. Starting with the first full chart week of 2025, the chart was renamed to Top Dance Albums to better reflect the cross-reference of dance titles on the ranking. As of the issue dated January 17, the current number-one album is ABBA Gold by ABBA. Additionally, there is a list of albums that achieved number-one status on the Billboard Top Dance/Electronic Albums Year-End chart.
